articles.title: Fauci Perjury Allegations Escalate: Rand Paul Demands DOJ Probe Into Gain-of-Function Lies Under Oath
articles.summary: Senator Rand Paul has formally referred Dr. Anthony Fauci to the Department of Justice for alleged perjury during 2021 congressional testimony, specifically over Fauci's repeated denials that NIH funded gain-of-function research at the Wuhan Institute of Virology. Documented NIH grant records contradict Fauci's sworn statements, and Paul argues the evidence is sufficient for a criminal referral. If prosecuted, this would represent the most significant accountability action taken against a senior U.S. public health official in modern history.

articles.title: Fauci's Secret Diary Exposed: Praised China, Trashed Trump, Lost Classified Files in Ransomware Attack
articles.summary: Newly released diary entries from Dr. Anthony Fauci reveal he privately praised Chinese health officials while publicly deferring to their pandemic narratives, and disparaged President Trump during the height of the COVID-19 crisis. The same records show Fauci lost a set of confidential government files in a ransomware hack — a security breach that was never disclosed to the public. The diary paints a damning picture of a public health czar whose private views and loyalties sharply contradicted his official posture.

articles.title: Doctors and Researchers Worldwide Revolt Against a Health System Engineered for Profit, Not Patients
articles.summary: India's Supreme Court has publicly condemned the exorbitant pricing and profit margins baked into the pharmaceutical supply chain, lending institutional weight to a growing global revolt among doctors and researchers who say Big Business has fully captured the health system. The commentary aggregates mounting international dissent against a model where treatment pricing, research priorities, and clinical guidelines are shaped by financial incentives rather than patient outcomes. The suppression of this debate in Western medical media is itself a symptom of the problem being described.

articles.title: Off-Patent Drug Ivermectin Showing Real Promise in Cancer — So Why Won't Oncology Acknowledge It?
articles.summary: Dr. William Makis, a Canadian oncologist and vocal dissident within the medical establishment, is making the case that cheap, off-patent drugs like ivermectin hold genuine therapeutic potential for cancer patients who have exhausted or been failed by standard-of-care treatments. The financial calculus is obvious: repurposed generics generate no patent revenue, giving pharmaceutical companies and the oncology complex zero incentive to fund trials or update protocols. Patients are being denied potentially life-extending options not because the science is absent, but because the profit motive isn't.

articles.title: Mebendazole vs. Gefitinib-Resistant Lung Cancer: Peer-Reviewed Data the Oncology Cartel Won't Promote
articles.summary: A peer-reviewed study published in PLOS ONE demonstrates that mebendazole — a decades-old, dirt-cheap antiparasitic — can disrupt tumor growth in gefitinib-resistant non-small cell lung cancer by targeting microtubule dynamics alongside EGFR signaling. This is precisely the class of repurposed, off-patent drug finding that gets quietly buried in academic journals while billion-dollar targeted therapies dominate oncology conferences and prescribing guidelines. The data exists; the system simply has no financial mechanism to translate it into standard of care.

articles.title: Plano COVID Testing Clinics to Pay $20M for Billing Fraud — The Pandemic Grift Nobody Wanted to Investigate
articles.summary: COVID testing clinics in Plano, Texas, operated by Heal 360, have agreed to pay $20 million to settle allegations that they systematically billed routine nasal swabs as full office visits, defrauding federal programs that were designed to serve the uninsured. This is a direct consequence of the no-accountability, flood-the-zone funding environment created during the pandemic — one that was entirely predictable and was predicted by critics of the emergency authorization and spending apparatus. The fraud was not an anomaly; it was a structural outcome of how the pandemic response was designed.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Hid iLet Device Safety Failures From Investors and the Public — FDA Compliance Was a Fiction
articles.summary: Beta Bionics faces a securities fraud class action after its stock collapsed 37% when concealed safety and efficacy problems with its iLet insulin-delivery device were finally disclosed — problems the company allegedly knew about while publicly claiming FDA compliance and commercial viability. This is the pattern: device and drug makers routinely manage the release of adverse safety data to protect stock price and market access, while patients using the product absorb the undisclosed risk. The securities lawsuit is the only mechanism forcing disclosure that regulators failed to compel.

articles.title: America's Medical Monopoly Has Spent a Century Suppressing Naturopathy — Here's What They Didn't Want You to Know
articles.summary: A detailed examination of naturopathic medicine's systematic suppression by the American medical establishment argues that licensing restrictions, insurance exclusions, and coordinated professional marginalization have been used as weapons to protect pharmaceutical-dependent allopathic medicine from competition rather than to protect patients. Razi Berry, founder of the Journal of Applied Natural Medicine, documents how practitioners offering dietary, botanical, and lifestyle-based interventions have faced career destruction and legal harassment not because their methods lack evidence, but because they threaten revenue streams. The monopoly on healing is enforced by law, not by science.

articles.title: Fauci Perjury Exposed: Rand Paul Demands DOJ Prosecute America's Most Powerful Doctor for Lying to Congress About Gain-of-Function

articles.title: Fauci's Private Diary Blows Open: Praised China, Sabotaged Trump, and Lost Classified Files in Ransomware Attack

articles.title: Off-Patent Cancer Drug Ivermectin Has Real Oncology Data — and Oncology Inc. Is Staying Quiet

Patients are being denied potentially viable options not because the science is absent, but because the profit motive is.

articles.summary: A peer-reviewed PLOS ONE study demonstrates that mebendazole, a decades-old antiparasitic drug costing pennies per dose, dramatically enhances cellular stress in gefitinib-resistant non-small cell lung cancer when combined with EGFR inhibition. This is precisely the kind of low-cost, off-patent combination therapy that receives no industry funding for large-scale trials because no pharmaceutical company can profit from it. The data exists — the clinical trials do not, and that gap is a business decision, not a scientific one.

articles.title: Antidepressant Harms Finally Getting a Hearing — But the Prescription Tsunami Rolls On
articles.summary: A critical analysis published in Spektrum examines the growing body of evidence that antidepressants are both overprescribed and inadequately studied for long-term harms, including dependency, sexual dysfunction, and emotional blunting that persists after discontinuation. Prescriptions have skyrocketed across the Western world while independent researchers documenting withdrawal syndromes and placebo-comparable efficacy in mild-to-moderate depression have faced professional marginalization. The system profits from lifetime prescriptions — not from cures.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Hid iLet Device Safety Failures From Investors — FDA Compliance Problems Now Triggering Securities Fraud Suits

Securities fraud class actions have now been filed, suggesting the company knew about device safety problems and concealed them from both the market and patients depending on the device. When medical device companies hide safety data from shareholders, they are hiding it from patients too.

Billions in COVID relief money vanished into schemes exactly like this while the public was told to trust the institutions administering it.

articles.title: America's Medical Monopoly Has Spent a Century Suppressing Naturopathic Medicine — Here's What They Buried
articles.summary: A deep dive into the structural suppression of naturopathic medicine details how the AMA and allied pharmaceutical interests systematically dismantled competing healing traditions through licensing boards, insurance exclusions, and coordinated media campaigns beginning in the early 20th century. Practitioners who reported clinical outcomes using nutrition, botanical medicine, and lifestyle intervention were denied hospital privileges, insurance reimbursement, and academic legitimacy — not because their results were inferior, but because their cures were not patentable. The monopoly was never about science; it was always about market control.
